title: onboard-signed-release-bundles-and-notes-assembler
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation:
Customers asked for tamper-evident release artifacts and predictable, machine-consumable release notes as part of model onboarding. Right now the registry stores model profiles and handwritten changelogs; this PR introduces a deterministic "release bundle" format that packages a model profile, evaluation snapshots, and a release-notes payload, plus an optional signature. The bundle is intended to be the single artifact uploaded to the registry and used by downstream deployers (Redwood Private installers, Dedicated infra, and partner integrations).

What this does (high level):
- Introduces `release-bundle` format (JSON + compressed assets) and a small manifest schema (bundle.v1) that contains: model_id, profile_id, variant_tags, eval_snapshots refs, notes (structured), and signature metadata (key-id, sig).
- Adds a CLI flow `redwood-mr bundle create --sign --notes-template PATH` that builds the bundle from model profile + eval outputs and optional user-supplied notes templates. Signing uses an edged KMS-backed keypair or local GPG-like key for local dev. Signatures are detached and stored inside the bundle manifest to allow both human and machine verification.
- Implements a `notes-assembler` service that converts profile deltas and selected eval metrics into structured change bullets and a compact machine field `summary_kv` suitable for automation (routing, rollout heuristics). The assembler supports templates with placeholders ({{perf.delta}}, {{latency.p95}}) and fallback heuristics when metrics are missing.
- Registry API endpoints: POST /bundles to upload bundles (with signature verification), and GET /bundles/:id to fetch signed bundles and raw notes. Existing onboarding endpoints are backward-compatible: if clients POST a legacy profile payload we synthesize a minimal bundle.v1.
- CI checks: `notes-lint`, `bundle-verify` (signature verification), and `e2e-bundle-install` which simulates a private installer fetching and installing a bundle and verifying signature and notes parsing.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Deterministic bundle structure: we intentionally avoid embedding ephemeral timestamps in the canonical manifest so generated signatures are stable across identical inputs. Metadata with environment specifics (build host, build id) can be stored in `meta.env` but is excluded from the signed canonical blob. This keeps signatures verifiable by customers who rebuild bundles from source assets.
- Signing model: supports two modes: KMS-backed (recommended for CI/production) and local key (dev). We do not implement a full web-of-trust here; customers who need stricter provenance should revoke keys at the registry level.
- Notes assembly: assembler generates both human-readable bullets and a structured `summary_kv` to be used by the Console for diff highlights and by rollouts to pick safer variants. We intentionally limit the assembler to metric diffs and model profile changes to avoid freeform schedule-writer complexity.

Backward compatibility:
- Old onboarding flows that push only model profiles still succeed; the backend synthesizes a bundle with an unsigned manifest and a `generated_notes` field. Consumers that expect signed bundles receive a 400 unless they explicitly opt-in to unsigned bundles (we surface this as a retention/opt-in toggle in the Console).

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for manifest canonicalization and signature verification (+ edge cases around array ordering).
- Notes-assembler unit tests covering templating, missing metrics, and multi-variant inputs.
- Integration CI job: `ci/bundle-e2e` that builds a sample bundle, pushes it to a test registry, then runs an installer container which verifies signature and parses notes. This is gated on the PR.
- Manual QA: Ran installer with bundles signed by local dev key and KMS key; validated the Console diff highlights display `summary_kv` correctly and that the deployment gate uses `perf.delta` to mark canary safety.

Ops and rollout plan:
- Feature flag `bundles.enabled` defaults to on for new registries; existing registries get a migration background job to synthesize bundles for recent model uploads (controlled ramp via rollout config).
- Short-term monitoring: bundle upload success rate, signature verification failures, notes-assembler errors, and Console render errors. Alert if signature verification error rate > 0.5% over 1h during rollouts.

Security considerations:
- Signature verification is enforced on /bundles ingestion when `require_signed` tenant setting is true. Key rotation is supported by storing key metadata and accepting signatures under previous keys for a configurable grace period.
- We do not ship private keys in the repo. KMS integration uses IAM roles configured per environment.

Checklist:
- [x] Manifest schema (bundle.v1) and canonicalization documented
- [x] CLI `bundle create` and `bundle verify` implemented
- [x] Registry endpoints to store and retrieve bundles
- [x] Notes assembler and templates
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] CI gating for bundle-e2e

Remaining items (follow-ups to be tracked separately):
- Add a Console UI for viewing signature key provenance and revocation list (ENG-7251).
- Expand notes assembler to include model qualitative tags (e.g., hallucination risk) once eval hooks are standardized.

References:
- Linear: ENG-7124, ENG-7251
- Support ticket SUP-1982 (customer asked for signed release artifacts)
- Related PRs: earlier profile and changelog automation work (existing repo history).

Files changed (high-level):
- cmd/redwood-mr/bundle.go (+ CLI flags and signer integration)
- pkg/registry/bundles/manifest.go (+ canonicalization and schema)
- pkg/registry/bundles/handler.go (+ POST/GET endpoints)
- internal/notes/assembler/assembler.go (+ templating engine, summary_kv generation)
- ci/workflows/bundle-e2e.yml (+ e2e job to verify bundles)
- integrations/kms/ (adapter and tests)

Release notes:
- Adds release bundle format (bundle.v1) and CLI tooling to create/verify signed bundles. Adds notes-assembler service to generate structured release notes and summary_kv for Console highlights. Backward compatible with legacy profile uploads.
